binding_note: sha256 of tracks/secp256k1-ecdlp/target-profile.json and tracks/classical-group-work-v2.json at repository revision 467130d867499e7bbca7479f0f72af0df115b282.
supersedes: submissions/secp256k1-ecdlp/automorphism-rho-v3 (rejected: epoch E=2^36 destroys merged pairs before 2^-64-density reporting; length-L cycle rate bound self-contradictory)
heuristics: H1: the canonical 32-adding walk on the (r-1)/6 automorphism classes has first-collision time approximating the birthday tail 1 - exp(-t^2/(2N)); supported classically, by Teske's r-adding-walk experiments, and by the toy run (0.545 vs 0.4845 ideal in the lag-free regime).

Cycle handling: zero-sum product-1 multiplier tuples over G6 enumerated exactly for L=2..8 (1, 2, 15, 60, 340, 1680, 9135; entry rates 2^-7.58 down to 2^-42.5 per step); a 16-state look-back detects every cycle of length 2..16 deterministically at its first return; lengths >= 17 are bounded by the trivial tuple count (entry <= 2^-80 per step) and fenced by the epoch E=2^44 (trapped fraction <= 2^-36). Distinguished points have density 2^-32, so the reporting interval 2^32 sits 2^12 below the epoch; the missed-report loss 2^-11 is computed by exact averaging and subtracted.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack with success probability lower bound 0.39 exactly at the protected threshold; all failures charged.
The distinguished-point table is a hard 2^95-slot allocation (2^102 bytes); overflow aborts with probability <= exp(-2^89) (Chernoff, ratio 1.07).
Standard cryptanalysis, not a novel attack; first qualified bound for this track under the protected cost model.
